A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a new class of plasmonic nanostructures that can be used for both photoacoustic imaging (PAI) and photothermal therapy in the first near infrared (NIR-I, 700-900 nm) and second near infrared (Nir-II, 1000-1350 nm) windows.
the plasmonic blackbody is a new class of compact plasmonic nanoabsorbers, which is different from the plasmonic nanoshells, nanorods, and nanocages.

we have demonstrated the use of a class of hyperbranched plasmonic blackbody materials for cancer theranosis in the NIR-I window, and that the improved Ptt outcome of NIR-II PTT over NIR-I PTT is primarily due to the higher maximum permissible exposure (MPE), not the deeper tissue penetration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compact plasmonic nanoabsorbers are a promising class of theranostic agents for cancer theranostics, particularly in combination with the NIR-II imaging window.
the NIR-II window has a higher potential for PTT than the NIR-I window, which may be due to the higher maximum permitted exposure (MPE).
a single plasmonic nanoabsorber can serve as a versatile theranostic agent for both NIR-I and NIR-II photoacoustic imaging, and photothermal therapy.
